summary: A bare React Native app for iOS and Android in TypeScript that owns its native projects, with a Swift Turbo Module example.
description: Start a React Native app with the community CLI instead of Expo, for teams that keep the Xcode and Android projects in the repository and write their own native code. The JavaScript side has React Navigation, validated settings, one error type with user-facing messages, structured logs and an error boundary. A local Turbo Module written in Swift reads the app version and OS, and one screen shows its answer with loading and error states. Jest with React Native Testing Library covers screens and navigation; an unsigned simulator build and an XCTest bundle cover the native side. The project is the app alone, and the sample module has no Android implementation yet.
seoDescription: A bare React Native app without Expo: TypeScript, React Navigation, a Swift Turbo Module, Jest screen tests and an iOS simulator build.

projectExamples.title: Bluetooth device companion
projectExamples.description: A React Native app that pairs with a company's own hardware through a native Bluetooth module and shows its readings on a few screens.

projectExamples.title: Staff app around a vendor SDK
projectExamples.description: An iPhone app for a company's staff that wraps a vendor's native iOS SDK in a Turbo Module and shows its results in React screens.

plain.whatItIs: A starter phone app for iPhone and Android written in TypeScript, where the project also keeps the native iOS and Android code and can add its own.
goodAt: Apps that need custom native code in Swift
Teams that want full control of the Xcode project
Testing screens and navigation without a device
notGoodAt: Apps that also need a server and database; use the Expo app with API stack.
Projects that want Expo's managed builds and updates.
